match.reason: The closest bank point, eng-simile-metaphor-personification, covers simile and metaphor as well as personification, so it is broader than this single-technique point, and the Year 11 symbolism point is at the wrong depth.

draft.title: Personification
card: Personification gives human actions or feelings to something that is not human. The thing might be an animal, an object, a place or the weather.
Example: "The old fridge groaned and complained all night." A fridge cannot groan or complain, but people can. The writer borrows those human actions.
The effect is to make a scene vivid, so the reader can picture it. It can also set a mood: a groaning fridge feels tired and grumpy.
To spot it, ask whether the verb or feeling belongs to a person. If a non-human thing is shown doing it, the writer is using personification.
draft.remember: Personification gives human actions or feelings to non-human things to build a picture or mood.

opts: The storm clouds frowned down on the sleepy town
The storm clouds were as dark as a bruise
The storm clouds covered the sky for hours
The storm clouds were an army of grey soldiers
a.why: Frowning is something people do, and clouds are shown doing it. The comparison with a bruise is a simile, and the army of soldiers is a metaphor. The plain sentence about covering the sky gives no human action.
a.clue: Look for something non-human doing what only a person can do.

b.q: Mia writes: "The empty playground waited patiently for the children to return." What effect does the personification have?
opts: It makes the playground seem lonely and hopeful
It shows the playground is bigger than it looks
It tells the reader exactly when the children return
It makes the playground sound loud and busy
b.why: Waiting patiently is a human feeling, so the playground seems to long for company. This creates a lonely, hopeful mood. The sentence says nothing about size, timing or noise.
b.clue: What would a person feel while waiting alone?

a.best: The storm clouds frowned down on the sleepy town

b.best: It makes the playground seem lonely and hopeful
